items.followUp: How do light and carbon dioxide contribute to photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Identifies chlorophyll’s role in capturing light energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chlorophyll absorbs or traps light energy.

rubric.why: Explains that light supplies the energy needed for photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that light provides energy for photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: Chlorophyll absorbs and traps light energy.
Light provides the energy needed to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose during photosynthesis.

items.followUp: How are enzymes used in the production of cheese?

rubric.why: Identifies the enzyme-assisted conversion of starch into sugars during brewing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes break down barley starch into sugars.

rubric.why: Explains how the sugars are used to produce alcohol in brewing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that yeast ferments the sugars to produce alcohol.

modelAnswer: In brewing, enzymes break down the starch in barley into sugars.
Yeast ferments these sugars to produce alcohol.

items.followUp: How can a change in temperature affect an enzyme's activity?

rubric.why: Recognizes that denaturation changes the enzyme’s structure or shape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that denaturation changes an enzyme’s structure or shape.

rubric.why: Connects the structural change to loss of enzyme function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the changed active site prevents the enzyme from working properly.

modelAnswer: Denaturation is a change in an enzyme’s structure or shape, usually caused by high temperature or an unsuitable pH.
The active site changes shape, so the enzyme loses its ability to catalyse the reaction.

items.followUp: State one health risk associated with eating too much saturated fat.

rubric.why: Identifies the effect of excess saturated fat on blood cholesterol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that excess saturated fat can raise blood cholesterol.

rubric.why: Names a related risk to cardiovascular health.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking this to coronary heart disease or blocked arteries.

modelAnswer: Eating too much saturated fatty acid can raise the level of cholesterol in the blood.
This increases the risk of blocked arteries and coronary heart disease.

items.followUp: Name the main route through which water vapour leaves a leaf.

rubric.why: Identifies transpiration as water loss in vapour form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that transpiration is the loss of water vapour.

rubric.why: Identifies where transpiration occurs, especially the stomata of leaves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that this loss occurs from aerial parts, mainly through leaf stomata.

modelAnswer: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant.
It occurs mainly through the stomata of leaves.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a genus name and a species name in binomial nomenclature?

rubric.why: Defines binomial nomenclature as a two-word naming system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each organism is given a scientific name consisting of two words.

rubric.why: Identifies the first word as the genus name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the first word as the genus.

rubric.why: Identifies the second word as the species name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the second word as the species name.

rubric.why: Explains that the naming system provides a common name used internationally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the system gives organisms a universal or internationally accepted name.

rubric.why: Explains how standard scientific names avoid confusion from different common names.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it avoids confusion caused by different local or common names.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature is the system of giving each organism a scientific name made up of two words.
The first word is the genus name.
The second word is the species name.
This system gives organisms a universal, internationally accepted name.
It avoids confusion caused by different common names for the same organism.

items.followUp: State the functions of vitamins D and B in the human body.

rubric.why: States the role of vitamin A in vision or eye health.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that vitamin A is needed for normal vision or healthy eyes.

rubric.why: Gives a related role or deficiency effect of vitamin A.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning healthy epithelial tissues or that vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness.

rubric.why: States an important role of vitamin C.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that vitamin C helps form collagen or supports wound healing.

rubric.why: Identifies a related deficiency effect or function of vitamin C.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy or that it helps keep gums healthy.

modelAnswer: Vitamin A is essential for normal vision and maintaining healthy epithelial tissues; its deficiency can cause night blindness.
Vitamin C is needed for collagen formation and wound healing; its deficiency causes scurvy and can lead to unhealthy gums.

items.followUp: Define an ecosystem and name one factor that can affect an organism's habitat.

rubric.why: Defines habitat as the place or environment where an organism lives.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a habitat as the natural place or environment in which an organism lives.

rubric.why: Adds that a habitat supports the organism’s needs or survival.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the habitat provides needs such as food or shelter, or supports survival or reproduction.

modelAnswer: A habitat is the natural place or environment in which an organism lives.
It provides the organism with the conditions and resources it needs, such as food and shelter.
